records.clause: or sooner when the app goes to the background
records.claimQuote: Clients batch events and send them every 10 seconds
records.rationale: An exception to the cadence that leaves the takeaway unchanged.

records.claimQuote: Each event carries an event name, a timestamp, an anonymous device id and, for signed-in users, an account id.
records.rationale: Without it every event would read as carrying an account id.

records.clause: The enrichment step uses the user service.
records.rationale: A mechanism statement; it limits nothing.

records.clause: If an account cannot be found
records.claimQuote: the event is passed on without account attributes
records.rationale: R4: the condition's most specific claim is its own consequent. X's link to u10 is kept as k5, the sentence-level exception.

records.clause: If an account cannot be found, the event is passed on without account attributes.
records.claimQuote: An enrichment step consumes the topic and adds account attributes, such as plan tier and region.
records.rationale: An exception to u10: some enriched events lack attributes, which matters for per-plan dashboards. u2_n7 joins carrier u2_n8 by a card arrow (linked); u2_a2 has no arrow to a carrier.

records.claimQuote: Enriched events are then written to the warehouse
records.rationale: On the u13 link the source settles it. Its Freshness section makes latency decision-relevant: launch reviews happen within 2 hours, and an hourly batch uses up to half of that. Without the clause, a reader relying on warehouse data for launches would act wrongly. The clash with u21's 'real time' is a source contradiction; it is not scored as a u21 limit, and u21 is judged not_a_condition (k7). Note: u6_n3, u6_a1 and g5 assert real-time freshness with no link to the hourly-batch carrier.
A (contradicted) claim, not a limit on one. X quoted the whole sentence; Y's minimal span is used.

records.clause: enrichment should avoid adding much traffic to it
records.claimQuote: The enrichment step uses the user service.
records.rationale: R1: X's deciding question is about the first half ('stay lightly loaded': forecast or requirement). The 'should avoid' half is a design constraint stated whichever way that is read. Building enrichment on the user service without it (per-event lookups) would break a stated constraint. u2_n7's arrow to u2_n11 is labelled 'constraint', which does not convey the clause, but it joins a carrier (linked). u2_n8 and u2_a2 have no such arrow.

records.claimQuote: Every event type must be registered
records.rationale: R4/R1: the clause sequences the registration rule it sits in. Following 'register every event type' without the ordering would let a client ship an unregistered type, and the collector would reject its events (u8). u16 is the most specific link; Y's u5 is the general flow.

records.clause: a breaking change requires a new version rather than an edit to the existing one
records.rationale: R1: editing a schema in place for a breaking change violates the stated rule.

records.clause: How long the aggregated tables are kept is TBD.
records.claimQuote: only aggregated tables are kept longer
records.rationale: An open item; the retention takeaway stands.

records.claimQuote: Raw events will be kept for 30 days and then deleted
records.readingA: claim: the table sets warehouse raw-event retention at 90 days, which limits or contradicts the 30-day statement; a reader acting on 30 days would mishandle deletion and access requests.
records.readingB: not_a_condition: a conflicting attribute in a component table; the draft is inconsistent rather than conditional.
records.decidingQuestion: Do u22 and u33 describe the same store (a drafting contradiction) or different stores (a scope on where 30 days applies), and which figure is intended?
records.rationale: Both annotators independently said ambiguous with the same readings; agreed ambiguous (cf. kn-02 c9 precedent). g6's takeaway restates the 30-day claim and counts as a claim card.

records.clause: the web app's sign-up and checkout events
records.claimQuote: The first dashboards will cover the onboarding funnel and weekly active accounts per plan tier.
records.readingA: claim (u14): phase 1 collects only web sign-up and checkout events, so the first dashboards (onboarding funnel, weekly active accounts per plan tier) cannot be fully built from phase 1; a reader would expect them.
records.readingB: set (u42): a scope on phase 1 that does not change the proposal's takeaway.
records.decidingQuestion: Are the first dashboards promised as a phase 1 deliverable?
records.rationale: The source never ties the first dashboards to a phase; not forced.

records.clause: once the mobile SDK is ready
records.rationale: R4: both links genuinely mislead without the clause, so one record per link (this one u36; k15 u5). Without it, phase 2 reads as unblocked.

records.clause: once the mobile SDK is ready
records.claimQuote: Client SDKs in the web and mobile apps send events to a collector service over HTTPS.
records.rationale: R4 second link: u5 presents mobile SDKs sending events as part of the design. Without the dependency, a reader expects mobile analytics from the start. No arrow joins the design frame g1 to the rollout carriers.

records.clause: no date has been set for it
records.rationale: A scheduling caveat; the takeaway stands.
R2: a hedged estimate; the source neither warns about it nor makes a decision turn on its precision. The takeaway is the same verified or not.

records.clause: The cost of running the pipeline has not been estimated yet.
records.claimQuote: We ask for approval to start phase 1
records.rationale: R3: the source never weighs cost against the benefit or the approval. It is listed under Rollout and is not even an open question. That answers Y's question (secondary open item): set. The cross-frame arrow g8->g9 'leads to' is not limiting.

records.clause: What happens to events the collector rejects: are they dropped, or kept somewhere for debugging?
records.claimQuote: rejects events that do not match a registered schema
records.rationale: An open question about rejected events; the rejection claim stands.

rejected.clause: We expect the user service to stay lightly loaded
rejected.reason: The rationale for the constraint in k8 (§2: rationale is not_a_condition). Read either as a forecast or as a requirement, its limiting force is the 'should avoid adding much traffic' clause, already recorded as k8.

notes: 19 records (9 claim, 6 set, 2 ambiguous, 2 not_a_condition). u12 yields k4 (intra-sentence) and k5 (exception to u10). u36 'once the mobile SDK is ready' yields one record per link (k14 u36, k15 u5) under R4.
